subject: reasoning
question: B, L, M, N, S, T and Z are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Z sits fourth to the right of B. Only two people sit between L and T when counted from the left of L. M sits third to the left of S. N is an immediate neighbour of S and T. How many people are there between Z and N when counted from the left of N?
solution:
**Given: **B, L, M, N, S, T and Z are sitting around a circular table facing the centre.

Z sits fourth to the right of B. Only two people sit between L and T when counted from the left of L.

M sits third to the left of S. N is an immediate neighbour of S and T.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1459bea22cbc859d3f2aa2433d1817a775e3a6b132b20c7e4f2720ed9f3aaab2.png] 

Thus, Only **FOUR **people are there between Z and N when counted from the left of N.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 3".**
